why: The symbol of Nagoya with the famous golden shachihoko fish on the roof. Walk the huge stone walls, see the rebuilt Hommaru Palace with gold painted screens, and eat at Kinshachi Yokocho next door.
One of the most important shrines in Japan, said to hold the sacred sword Kusanagi. Huge old camphor trees, a quiet forest in the city, and the famous hitsumabushi eel shops nearby.
Big red temple at the start of Osu shopping streets. Pigeons, a flea market on the 18th and 28th of every month, and a giant paper lantern.
Covered streets full of street food, anime and game shops, second-hand clothes, electronics and cheap eats. The best place in Nagoya to wander when you're bored.
A glass "spaceship" roof with water on top. Walk around the roof for a view of the TV tower, best after dark when it lights up. Shops and the Ghibli and Pokémon stores are below.
Japan's oldest TV tower, now a national cultural property. City views from the Sky Deck, and it glows at night.
Open-air rooftop on the 44th–46th floors near Nagoya Station. One of the best night views in the city.
Free window view over Nagoya Station from the 15th floor, plus restaurants and the Hands store.
Samurai treasures of the Owari Tokugawa lords: swords, armour, Noh masks and the famous Tale of Genji scrolls (shown a few weeks a year).
A traditional garden with a pond, a waterfall and koi. Beautiful in autumn leaves and peony season. Next to the Tokugawa Art Museum.
Big Japanese garden shaped like the landscape of the Chubu region, with a tea house. Lovely autumn light-ups.
Home of one of the world's largest planetariums (the big silver ball), an indoor tornado, a 4 m lightning show and a minus 30°C deep-freeze room.
Modern art in Shirakawa Park, including Modigliani and Mexican art. Good with the science museum next door.

en: Toyota Commemorative Museum of Industry and Technology
ja: トヨタ産業技術記念館
why: Old red-brick Toyota factory with working looms and car-making machines. Staff run real demonstrations. Great even if you don't love cars.
Red-brick factory chimneys, lawns and a craft centre where you can paint your own plate.
Real bullet trains and the record-breaking maglev you can walk into. Simulators let you drive a shinkansen.

ja: レゴランド・ジャパン
why: Lego theme park with rides and a miniature Japan built from Lego. Next to Maker's Pier for food.
Colourful outdoor shopping and food area by the sea next to LEGOLAND.
One of Japan's biggest aquariums: orcas, belugas, a big dolphin show and penguins.
Small amusement park with a big Ferris wheel that lights up the port at night.
Walk through a real ice-breaker ship that went to Antarctica, with the crew rooms still set up.
White sail-shaped building with a maritime museum and a 53 m observation deck over the port.
Huge zoo with koalas, the famous "handsome" gorilla Shabani, and a glass botanical greenhouse from 1937.
134 m tower on a hill. On clear days you can see the Japanese Alps; at night the city lights.
Big hilly park with 1,000 cherry trees, forest walks and ponds. Good for a bike ride.
Large park north of the castle with a running track, flower garden and the tonarino cafés.
Long park through Sakae with lawns, cafés and shops (RAYARD), right under the TV tower.
Nagoya's oldest Western-style park with a fountain pavilion and one of the city's top cherry blossom spots.
Green park with the science and art museums inside.
Nagoya's history from ancient times to today, with good special exhibitions.
Edo-period street of old merchant houses famous for shibori tie-dye. Try making your own at a workshop.
The only temple in Japan not belonging to any one sect, built to hold remains of the Buddha given by Thailand. Market on the 21st of each month.
Five-storey wooden pagoda in a forest in Yagoto. Beautiful autumn leaves.
Family temple of the Owari Tokugawa lords with a huge old gate.
Temple inside the Osu streets with a mechanical dragon show (Hakuryu) several times a day.
Small colourful shrine to Tokugawa Ieyasu near the castle.
Old shrine next to Toshogu, said to be over 1,000 years old.
Old city shrine hidden between the buildings of Sakae.
2.5 km riverside path lined with cherry trees. Famous in spring and nice for a bike ride any time.
Shrine on a hill near Kakuozan with a "lovers' tree" people visit for good luck in love.
Temple with a big green Buddha statue in the woods near Motoyama.
The biggest keyhole-shaped burial mound in Aichi, in Atsuta Park.
A Ferris wheel built into the side of a building in central Sakae. Also SKE48's theatre inside.

ja: ジェイアール名古屋タカシマヤ
why: Big department store above Nagoya Station with a famous basement food hall.
Fashion mall in Sakae with good restaurants on the top floors.
Nagoya's classic department store, one of the biggest in Japan.
Department store in the middle of Sakae with a rooftop amusement corner.
Youth fashion, character shops and pop-up stores.
Huge mall with a cinema, food court and lots of shops.
Big AEON mall with a cinema and food court near Atsuta Shrine.

ja: ららぽーと名古屋みなとアクルス
why: Big modern mall by the canal with a cinema and lots of restaurants.

ja: コメ兵 名古屋本店
why: Giant second-hand shop for brand bags, watches, clothes and cameras.

ja: まんだらけ 名古屋店
why: Second-hand manga, figures, games and rare collector items.

ja: バンテリンドーム ナゴヤ
why: Home of the Chunichi Dragons baseball team. Big concerts too.

ja: 愛知芸術文化センター
why: Art museum, concert halls and a free view terrace on the 10th floor in Sakae.
Grand red-brick old court building from 1922 with a stunning stained glass staircase.
Castle-style city hall from 1933, a national cultural property.
Western-style house of Japan's first actress, Sadayakko, with stained glass.
Traditional Noh stage near the castle. The lobby and exhibits are often free.
Nagoya's classic kabuki and musical theatre.
Old-style rakugo and manzai comedy theatre in Osu.

ja: ミッドランドスクエア シネマ
why: Big cinema at Nagoya Station.

ja: あつた蓬莱軒 本店
why: The home of hitsumabushi: grilled eel on rice you eat three ways. Expect a queue.

ja: 矢場とん 矢場町本店
why: Famous miso-katsu: pork cutlet with sweet red miso sauce.

ja: 世界の山ちゃん 本店
why: Peppery tebasaki chicken wings, Nagoya's favourite bar snack.
Birthplace of "Taiwan ramen", a very spicy minced-meat noodle soup only found in Nagoya.

ja: 山本屋総本家 本家
why: Thick udon boiled in a clay pot with red miso.

ja: コメダ珈琲店 菊井店
why: The very first Komeda's. Order coffee before 11:00 and get free toast and egg (morning service).
Famous for crazy dishes like sweet matcha spaghetti. A legendary "challenge" café.

ja: 喫茶 コンパル 大須本店
why: Old Nagoya coffee shop famous for fried shrimp sandwiches and iced coffee.
Edo-style food street at the castle gates with Nagoya local dishes.
Old stone-walled merchant storehouse street, now cafés and restaurants.
Retro covered shopping street with local cafés and shops near Shikemichi.
Stylish open-air shops and cafés on a hill.

ja: ドン・キホーテ 栄本店
why: Crazy packed discount store open late, everything from snacks to costumes.
Morning fish market near Nagoya Station with seafood restaurants.

ja: 竜泉寺の湯 名古屋守山本店
why: Big super-sento hot spring with outdoor baths on a hill and many sauna types.
Famous sauna with a forest-themed cold "Finnish" room. Open 24 hours.
Huge park with forest trails, a lake with boats, a dinosaur zone and cycling.

ja: 東谷山フルーツパーク
why: Fruit orchards with seasonal picking and a tropical greenhouse.
Tidal flat for birdwatching with a free visitor centre.
Big riverside park with a rose garden, boating and cycling paths.
Forest park known for fireflies in early summer.
Park with a big flower garden and lavender in early summer.
Birthplace of Toyotomi Hideyoshi, with a big red torii and a small museum.
Free museum about Toyotomi Hideyoshi and Kato Kiyomasa, both born nearby.
Free hands-on electricity museum with experiments.
Big concert and sports arena.

ja: 名古屋スポーツセンター
why: Ice skating rink where top Japanese figure skaters trained.
Sports park with stadiums and a running course.

ja: 真宗大谷派名古屋別院
why: Large temple on the site of an old castle; big markets some days.
Big temple in Tachibana, quiet and spacious.
Shrine next to the castle area.
One of the Four Kannon of Owari, with a cute legend about a straw hat.
Old hilltop temple with a view, next to the Ryusenji no Yu hot spring.
Temple with over 1,200 small wooden Buddha statues carved by Enku.

ja: ラウンドワン 名古屋中川店
why: Bowling, arcade, karaoke and Spo-Cha (all-you-can-play sports) in one building.

en: Bic Camera Nagoya JR Gate Tower
ja: ビックカメラ 名古屋JRゲートタワー店
why: Electronics, games and gadgets with tax-free counters.
Underground street at Nagoya Station's west side with Nagoya food all in one place.
Underground shopping street linking Sakae station.

ja: 宮きしめん 神宮店
why: Flat kishimen noodles inside the Atsuta Shrine grounds.
Walk along the historic canal that carried stone to build the castle.
Long flat riverside path, perfect for a bike ride away from cars.
Farm park with animals and famous weeping plum blossoms in March.
Seaside area with the aquarium, ship Fuji, and harbour views.
Hilly old street of small cafés, bakeries and shops leading to Nittaiji Temple.
Antique and flea market at Osu Kannon on the 18th and 28th of each month.
One of only 12 original castles in Japan, on a cliff over the Kiso River. Old castle town street below.
Over 60 real Meiji-era buildings moved here, including Frank Lloyd Wright's old Imperial Hotel lobby.
Houses from around the world with world food to try.

ja: ナガシマスパーランド
why: Big roller coaster park with the Steel Dragon 2000, next to an outlet mall and hot spring.
Studio Ghibli worlds in the Expo park: Satsuki and Mei's house, the Grand Warehouse and more. Tickets must be booked.
About 140 classic cars from around the world.

ja: あいち航空ミュージアム
why: Real planes including the YS-11 and the Zero fighter, next to Nagoya Airfield.
Famous fertility shrine with a big festival every 15 March.
Winding lanes lined with clay pipes and pottery kilns near the airport.
One of Japan's best autumn leaf valleys, with a river and a red bridge.
Huge Expo 2005 park with cycling, a big playground, and Ghibli Park inside.

ja: イオンモールナゴヤドーム前
why: Big mall next to the Dome with a cinema.
Twin towers over Nagoya Station with restaurant floors and window views.
Modern area south of the station with Global Gate tower and its 34th-floor sky lobby.
The oldest glass greenhouse in Japan (1937), a national cultural property.
Big quiet library in Tsuruma Park. Good when you just want calm.

en: Nagoya Science Museum Planetarium Brother Earth
ja: 名古屋市科学館 プラネタリウム
why: 35 m dome, one of the biggest planetariums in the world, with live narration.
hours: Several shows a day, closed Mon

why: Swords, mirrors and treasures given to Atsuta Shrine over 1,000 years.

ja: 名古屋城 本丸御殿
why: Gold painted walls and ceilings of the lord's palace, rebuilt with original methods.
Electronics, PC parts and maid cafés: Nagoya's mini Akihabara.
Seaside lawn to watch planes, ships and sunset near Maker's Pier.

ja: 稲永ビジターセンター
why: Visitor centre and hide for bird watching at Fujimae tidal flat.
Miles of underground shops and cheap food around Nagoya Station.
Long underground shopping street under Hisaya Odori Park.

ja: ミッドランドスクエア
why: Luxury shops and restaurants in Nagoya's tallest building.
Cafés, a running station and shops next to Meijo Park.
Free sky lobby view on the 34th floor of Global Gate tower.
New arena in Meijo Park for sumo, basketball and concerts.
"Path of Culture": old Western houses and samurai homes between the castle and Tokugawaen.
Sakae's south side (Sakae Minami) is busiest at night with bars and lights.
